title: Token-aware SLO ledger and staged soft-breaker policy for bursty conversational endpoints
creator: Arielle Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood's conversational/chat routes (short-turn and multi-turn) are increasingly bursty and token-heavy. Current SLOs are defined mostly in availability/latency terms and do not account for token economics or input-class driven quality regressions. This ticket establishes a per-endpoint SLO ledger that accounts for token-based error-budgeting, defines staged soft-breaker behaviors, and specifies regional reservation preemption to avoid noisy multi-region failovers during short, intense bursts.

Scope:
- Define canonical SLIs and SLOs for conversational endpoints (route-level + model-variant).
- Express error budgets in token-units (tokens/month) in addition to request-based budgets.
- Specify staged soft-breaker thresholds and the actions at each stage (variant deprioritization, regional reservation, tenant-level shedding).
- Deliver dashboards, alert rules, and a runnable runbook for SRE/Oncall.

Goals / Acceptance Criteria:
- SLO ledger covering availability, latency (tail), success/quality, and token-burn budget for 3 endpoint classes: short-turn chat, long-turn chat, and completion-style conversational APIs.
- Concrete burn-rate triggers and actions defined so automated controllers can act (no ambiguous language).
- Dashboards in Console (per-route + per-variant) showing current SLI, budget remaining (tokens and requests), forecasted burn-rate, and suggested remediation.
- Runbook with clearly specified steps, owners, and post-incident data collection checklist.

Proposed SLI / SLO definitions (examples):
1) Availability SLI (route): fraction of requests that return a successful 2xx within the route's SLA window.
   - Short-turn chat (interactive routes): SLO = 99.9% window monthly.
   - Long-turn chat (sessioned generation): SLO = 99.5% monthly.
2) Tail Latency SLI (model-variant): p99 generation latency measured from request received to last-token-emitted (excluding backpressure queuing beyond configured soft-queue).
   - Short-turn: p99 < 800ms.
   - Long-turn: p99 < 2000ms.
3) Quality SLI (model-variant): pass-rate on a promptset of regression checks tied to the route (evaluated hourly/rolling 24h).
   - SLO: >= 97% for critical routes; >= 95% for non-critical.
4) Token-budget SLI (route): tokens consumed by this route in a month relative to an allocated token allowance. Error budget is expressed in tokens.
   - Baseline allocation is derived from 90th-percentile historical token usage for the previous quarter plus growth buffer.
   - SLO: retain >= 20% of token budget at month end (i.e., avoid burning entire allowance early).

Token-pricing-aware error budget and burn-rate model:
- Error budget is represented in two currencies: requests and tokens. Controllers evaluate both; exceeding either triggers mitigation.
- Define token burn-rate = tokens_used_per_minute / token_allowance_per_minute. Use an EWMA over 10 minutes to smooth spikes.
- Burn rate thresholds:
  - Warning: > 0.6 (notify PM/SRE, surface in console)
  - Level-1 soft-breaker: > 1.0 sustained for 5m (demote lower-priority model variants, reduce max generation length by 20%).
  - Level-2 regional reservation: > 1.8 sustained for 2m (preemptively reserve capacity in lower-cost region and divert bursty tenant traffic there if allowed by policy).
  - Level-3 hard-shedding: > 3.0 (initiate tenant-level shedding based on priority matrix).

Staged soft-breaker behavior (actions):
- Soft-breaker L1 (variant & prompt heuristics): reduce max_tokens, enable condensed decoding, switch to quantized variant where quality delta acceptable.
- Soft-breaker L2 (regional reservation): mark low-priority tenants as eligible for cross-region diversion, create temporary reservation slices in target region, and throttle new session creation in the origin region.
- Soft-breaker L3 (tenant shedding): drop (HTTP 429) or deprioritize requests for non-critical tenants/routes following the configured priority matrix.

Observability / Dashboards / Alerts:
- Per-route ledger widget: current SLI, monthly token budget, tokens remaining, burn-rate EWMA, projected exhaustion time.
- Per-variant tail-latency heatmap and quality trend.
- Alerts: burn-rate warning (level: page), L1 automated-action (notify + annotation), L2 automated-action and owner page, L3 oncall page + escalation.

Runbook (summary):
1) If burn-rate > 0.6: open SLO investigation ticket, annotate route ledger, DM PM and SRE.
2) If automated L1 actions occur: verify variant fallback health, confirm quality SLI is within tolerance.
3) If L2 triggered: run cross-region checklist (data residency check, KMS key availability, routing and cost impact), and contact Platform Ops.
4) If L3 triggered: follow tenant-priority ledger to shed traffic; notify affected customers and CS/AE teams.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (two-week): implement ledger + metrics, surface dashboards and non-blocking alerts for three pilot routes (short-turn chatbot, mail-summarize, agents-chat).
- Phase 2 (one month): deploy automated L1 controller for pilot routes; test in staging with synthetic bursts.
- Phase 3 (6 weeks): enable L2 regional reservation automation behind a feature flag and test in limited production with canary tenants.

Data & measurement notes:
- Token accounting must be precise and folded into billing pipeline; reconcile once per day.
- Quality SLI relies on a curated promptset per route; own the promptset as part of the route manifest.

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Whether to express token budgets as absolute tokens/month or as cost-dollar equivalents tied to dynamic price tiers (we recommend tokens for precision).
- Cross-region reservation policy: propose opt-in per-tenant due to compliance concerns; need legal signoff for any automatic cross-region diversion.
